beliefs.practice: Read the DocumentDB connection string only from an environment variable (DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime, never commit it to source, and load it into Mongoose with explicit options (e.g., maxPoolSize, serverSelectionTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) rather than concatenating credentials into code or config files.
Use Mongoose/Mongo driver connection pooling and set a bounded pool size (e.g., maxPoolSize: 50) and keepAlive/heartbeat settings to avoid connection churn from short-lived Lambda-like processes.
Never log secrets or the full connection URI; use .env.example with placeholders and store real credentials in a secrets manager (Azure Key Vault or equivalent) for production.
Use least-privilege credentials: create a database user that only has readWrite on sample_fintech_20 (not admin) and use those scoped credentials from the app instead of a cluster-level admin key.

Model cache documents with explicit fields: cacheKey (string, indexed), value (any), fetchedAt (Date), expiresAt (Date), staleAfterAt (Date), and optional refreshing (boolean/timestamp) so TTL + stale-while-revalidate logic is deterministic.

Create a TTL index on expiresAt with expireAfterSeconds: 0 (i.e., db.collection.createIndex({expiresAt:1},{expireAfterSeconds:0})) so documents are eligible for automatic removal when expiresAt <= now; keep a separate staleAfterAt for stale-window handling.

Implement stale-while-revalidate by: on request, if now < expiresAt return fresh; else if now < staleAfterAt return stale immediately and kick a background refresh; else block and refresh synchronously. Use an atomic findOneAndUpdate to set a refreshing flag to dedupe concurrent refreshes.
Use atomic upsert operations (findOneAndUpdate with upsert:true and $setOnInsert for immutable fields) when inserting or refreshing cache documents to avoid race conditions and stampedes.
Guard background refresh with a short 'refreshing' lock set via findOneAndUpdate (e.g., set refreshingUntil timestamp) and include a fallback timeout so a stuck worker cannot lock refreshes forever.

Index the cache key path(s) used by lookup queries (for example {cacheKey:1} or compound {tenantId:1, cacheKey:1}); for high-cardinality dynamic keys consider a hashed index on cacheKey to keep index size and write amplification reasonable.

Avoid collection-wide scans in vector or metadata filters: ensure any non-vector predicates (tenantId, endpoint, date ranges) are backed by indexes so vector-scoring only runs over a small candidate set.

When using vector search features, store normalized vectors, limit dimensionality to what the index supports, and set query-time HNSW parameters (efSearch/ef) appropriately to trade latency vs recall; persist index config (M, efConstruction) at index-creation time.

Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient network or server errors (e.g., MongoNetworkError, MongoServerSelectionError), but avoid retrying non-idempotent requests blindly—use idempotent upserts for cache writes when retries are expected.

Tune timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS, connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) and enable monitoring of connection pool metrics to detect exhausted pools; prefer long-lived connections for servers with predictable traffic.

Provision adequate throughput for the cache collection (or use autoscale) so background refresh storms or bursts don't trigger throttling—monitor RU/s or the provider's equivalent and set alerts for throttling/429s.

Instrument cache operations with metrics (hit rate, miss rate, refresh duration, background refresh failures) and enable slow query and index usage logging so you can detect missing indexes and hot keys.

Avoid storing large binary blobs in cache documents; if responses are large, store them in an object store and store just metadata and a reference in DocumentDB to keep document sizes small and indexable.

Encrypt sensitive fields at rest or use provider-managed encryption; for highly sensitive PII consider client-side field-level encryption where supported by the MongoDB driver, and never rely only on network/TLS for data protection.
